newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian farmers threaten stoppage, demand cash.
newsitem.headline: Serbian farmers threaten stoppage, demand cash.

text.p: Serbian farmers said on Thursday they would interrupt spring sowing on around 2.37 million hectares next week to protest about overdue payments and the state's neglect of argiculture.
"We will block main roads and border crossings for five hours starting noon next Wednesday," said Jordan Konstantinovic of the Jugoagrar producers association.
Farmers are also demanding that all frozen bank accounts be unblocked, debt rescheduling, bans on food imports and favourable loans for financing the spring campaign.
"We have self-financed our production during four years of sanctions and prevented people from going hungry by keeping our prices below the cost levels," Konstantinovic told Reuters.
Agricultural debt has built up to some two billion dinars.
Producers warned earlier they would boycott the state's ambitious spring sowing programme unless money was found and they were paid in full for the 1996 crop.

The government said in late January it would make extra efforts to clear its outstanding 800 million dinars debt to farmers by mid-March in view of the overall cash shortage and expected money to be used for the spring campaign.
Industry officials saw the move as insufficient and said the money would not reach producers on time.

"The accounts of most agricultural co-operatives and enterprises are blocked because of insolvency. Employees have not received their wages for months," said Ljiljana Vasic, the head of the association of agricultural co-operatives of Vojvodina.
"What was 800 million last autumn is not the same in March or April this year. And even if some money does arrive it never reaches the real producer," she said.
The government has offered fuel, seeds and fertiliser to clear its debt.
"What we need is cash. We cannot pay our bills or buy medicine with fertiliser," Konstantinovic said.
